October 19, 2026 · 117 careers checked per model

Are we missing a sensible match?

Review of all 28 models that originally had no option covering their lifestyle at starting pay.

5models with recovered options
21starting-pay shortfalls remain
2profiles need more interest evidence

The current chart has 23 public models without coverage, down from 28. No wages, budgets, answers, scores or Top matches were changed. The six owner-only models already had a covering option and retain private storage.

What changed

  • Career-specific evidence now survives an incomplete broad-field check. Six or more focused task answers can produce a related option when the wider interest pattern is less strong. Aisha’s analysis work and Linh’s animation choices were being missed.
  • Related search follows the Top matches actually displayed. The older engine sometimes left tied careers out of its short list. This hid branches from Gabriel, Imani and Audrey even though those careers appeared on the new results page.
  • Related ideas remain unconfirmed. Imani’s physical-product design and Audrey’s business roles need new daily-work trials. Gabriel needs to compare clinical rehabilitation and psychological assessment with teaching. A covering salary does not establish interest or readiness.

Catalog gaps worth investigating

Technical writing, purchasing/buying and training/development deserve dedicated coverage. Accurate explanations, stock/product comparisons and teaching can justify investigating these distinct duties. Their own Austin entry wages, prerequisites and focused questions must be verified before counting them as covering options. National median pay is not a starting-pay substitute; training/development and some technical-writing routes require relevant experience.

Method, limits & reproducible evidence
  1. Review current interests, recent biography, field preferences and career-specific answers for every baseline case.
  2. Independently calculate first-paid-stage lifestyle budgets across all 117 current careers, excluding roles requiring prior experience.
  3. Compare higher-pay alternatives with actual interest evidence; do not treat a correlation or salary alone as a justified choice.
  4. Repair only two exclusion paths: use the supported Top matches displayed on the page as related-search seeds; retain strongly evidenced task-related options despite incomplete broad field confirmation.
  5. Task-related options require completed field follow-ups, at least six distinct selected question groups, three refinements, four focused answers, two task domains, positive destination-field evidence, correlation at least 0.20, and no route/clinical/field conflict. Flat profiles remain open.
  6. Keep core scores, official answers, Top matches, pay references and budget assumptions unchanged.

These are fictional-model software scenarios. The three catalog follow-ups are not included in the 117-career affordability scan. Clinical and experience requirements remain distinct from transferable interests. The fixes were informed by both development and previously held-out cases. Reusing them is regression testing, not independent holdout validation of this revised layer. Fresh untouched cases are needed for that. These checks do not establish accuracy or outcomes with real students.
